brief:
Tonight is Pull A, and it is the last hard session of this block. The deload starts tomorrow, Monday 21 September, and runs through Sunday the 27th at lighter weights and fewer sets. You trained Push A last night, so this is a back-to-back day with deadlifts on it — that is the one thing to know walking in.

Deadlift is where the real decision was. Your last Pull A, on 10 September, you did three sets: 235 for 5, then 255 for 4, then 255 for 4. The slot asks for four sets of five to six reps, so those top sets came in under the range and the fourth never happened. Left alone, the app was going to ask you for 255 for 6, three times — beating a night you did not finish. It is not asking that. Same weights, four sets, and the target is five reps, not six: 235 for 5, then 255 for 5, 5 and 5. Your recovery trainer wanted to leave it at three sets because you lifted last night. I ruled against that, and here is why: you did four sets of deadlifts on 24 July, 1 August, 18 August and 28 August. Four is your normal, not a stretch, and 10 September is the only short one in the record. Whatever the fourth set costs you, tomorrow is a rest day and the whole week after it is light.

One lift goes up. Lat pulldown: you pulled 93 for a clean 10 on your middle set on 10 September, then dropped back to 88 for the third. If 93 is good for 10 once, it is your working weight — so 93 on all three sets, aiming for 10, then 9, then 8. The 150 you were pulling in August was the old gym's machine and does not transfer.

The rest hold. Cable row stays at 55 for 10, four sets — and be aware nobody has a real number for this slot at this gym, because on 10 September you did one-armed dumbbell rows instead. If you get on an actual cable row tonight, just use whatever gives you 10 to 12 and log it; that becomes the starting point. Curls stay at the 50 barbell for 10, 10 and 9 — you got 10, 10, 8 last time, so the job is one more rep on the last set. Hammer curls stay at 35 for 12, 11, 11. Face pulls stay at 27.5 for 14 then 13, still two sets, and they are staying two — you have told me that three times and I am not asking again.

Two things off the gym floor. Nobody has weighed you since 23 August — 207 pounds, 28 days ago, with the show 162 days out. Deload week is the easy week to get back on the scale. And your whole log contains exactly one cardio session: 15 minutes on an elliptical on 21 July, 61 days ago. If conditioning is happening and just not getting logged, log it. If it is not happening, that is the biggest gap between here and March.

Last thing. There are two Yes/No cards waiting for you, both about Legs A, and neither touches tonight. You should know what they are before you tap: both of them undo something you already said yes to. On 23 August you agreed to take Legs A leg curl up from three sets to four; on 16 August you agreed to take the split squat up from two to three. Your program trainer looked at what you have actually run since and wants to write both back down. That is a fair observation — you did two sets of leg curl on 13 September, and two split squats — but it is also me asking you to reverse yourself on thin evidence, one Legs A night each. Both cards are written so that saying no keeps what you originally chose. If the four sets were the right idea and the last Legs A was just a short night, say no and keep them.

Nobody has a real cable-row number for you at this gym. On 10 September you did one-armed dumbbell rows in that slot. Tonight's 55 for 10 is a placeholder — if you use the actual cable row, log whatever gives you 10 to 12 and that becomes the baseline.

No Yes/No card exists for either, because the plan has no barbell-curl or one-arm-row entry to swap to — fixing that needs a code change I am not allowed to make.

Your recovery trainer read all of your notes by hand again this morning and found no pain, soreness, joint trouble or injury anywhere. It has to read them by hand because the automatic pain list is still broken — its only ever hit is your 23 August lateral-raise sentence, matched because 'number' contains 'numb'.

Tonight's two Yes/No cards both UNDO something you accepted a month ago — leg curl going up to four sets on 23 August, the split squat going up to three on 16 August. Your program trainer flagged that you have not been hitting either number since. Both cards are written so that saying no keeps what you already chose.

Three trainers reported. Two disagreements, both settled for the progression trainer — the deadlift's fourth set and the lat pulldown going to 93. No vetoes, and nobody raised a pain or injury objection. The program trainer's two asks were caught as reversals of your own earlier answers and rewritten to say so rather than being dropped.

proposals.why: Read this before you answer: on 23 August you said yes to taking Legs A leg curl UP from three sets to four, to stop the front of your leg out-earning the back. You have run Legs A once since — 13 September — and did two sets. This card asks whether to write it back down to three, the number Legs B already asks. Saying no keeps the four you chose.

Same kind of question: on 16 August you said yes to taking the split squat UP from two sets to three. You did three on 20 August, right after you agreed, then two again on 13 September. This card asks whether to write it back to two. Saying no keeps the three you chose, and the honest read is that you have managed it once.

overrides.reason: Same weights as 10 September, but all four sets and five reps is the target, not six. You got 255 for 4 and 4 that night and never did the fourth set, so repeating it at six reps would be asking you to beat a session you did not finish.

You pulled 93 for a clean 10 on your middle set on 10 September, so 93 is proven here — put it on all three sets instead of dropping back to 88. The 150 from August was the old gym's machine and does not carry over.

You have never logged a cable row at this gym — on 10 September you did one-armed dumbbell rows at 55, and the 105 in your history is the old gym's machine. 55 for 10, four sets, is the only number anyone can stand behind. On a real cable row, use whatever gives you 10 to 12 and log it.
This is the 50-pound barbell you curled on 10 September, not 50-pound dumbbells. You got 10, 10 and 8, so three straight tens is not earned yet — same bar, one more rep on the last set.

35 at this gym gave you 11, 11 and 10 on 10 September, just short of the twelves you were getting before the move. Stay at 35 and chase the reps back rather than adding weight on the last hard night of the block.

You did 15 and 15 at 27.5 on 3 September, then 13s on the 10th and 13s again at 27 on the 15th. The weight is right and the reps slid, so hold 27.5 and aim for 14 on the first set. Still two sets — that is settled.

dissent.progression: Hold the weights but restore the missing fourth set and target five reps, because 10 September fell below the slot's floor rather than topping it.
dissent.recovery: Keep it at three sets — he trained a 66-minute Push A last night, this is the last hard night of a four-week build, and he already self-trimmed to three on 10 September.
dissent.why: Recovery's fatigue reading is fair but its one supporting fact is wrong in context. I checked every Pull A in the record: he did four sets of deadlifts on 24 July, 1 August, 18 August and 28 August. 10 September is the only three-set night there has ever been, so four sets is his normal and not a new demand. Against that, the cost of the extra set lands on a rest day tomorrow and a deload week after it — this is the cheapest possible night to spend it. I also took progression's rep target of five rather than the app's six, which is the real protection here: 255 gave him four reps twice on 10 September, and asking six would have been the actual over-reach.

dissent.progression: Put the proven 93 on all three sets at 10, 9 and 8 instead of sliding back to 88 on the third.
dissent.recovery: Hold — three steady sets, no push on the last hard night before a deload.
dissent.why: Recovery is arguing set count here, and set count is not in dispute: both seats say three. On the weight it had nothing to argue with, because its evidence carries no loads at all. Progression's case stands on its own: he pulled 93 for a clean 10 on 10 September, so 93 is not a reach, it is a number he has already produced at this gym. The descending 10/9/8 target asks for one rep more in total than the 10/10/9 he actually did, which is the smallest honest step available.
